name: Microsoft

summary.text: Microsoft Corporation is a publicly traded software and cloud-computing company. It holds the Army's original 2018 IVAS headset agreement (transferred to Anduril in 2025), is a provider on the Pentagon's Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability contract, and is the largest outside investor in OpenAI, holding about 27 percent of OpenAI Group PBC after the October 2025 recapitalization. In 2024 the U.S. Cyber Safety Review Board found that the 2023 Storm-0558 intrusion into Exchange Online was preventable and that Microsoft's security culture was inadequate. In 2025 Microsoft said it had ceased some cloud and AI services to a unit of Israel's Ministry of Defense after a review.

facts.claim: In November 2018 the Army awarded Microsoft an Other Transaction Agreement worth up to $22 billion over ten years to develop the Integrated Visual Augmentation System (IVAS). In April 2025 the Army approved a contract novation transferring the IVAS production contract from Microsoft to Anduril. A July 2026 GAO report, summarized by CRS, said the Army determined none of the 10,000 developed IVAS units will be fielded.
facts.quote: In November 2018, the Army awarded an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA), worth up to $22 billion over 10 years, to Microsoft for the development of IVAS.

facts.claim: The Cyber Safety Review Board's review of the summer 2023 Microsoft Exchange Online intrusion by the China-linked group Storm-0558 (report dated March 20, 2024, released April 2, 2024) concluded the intrusion was preventable, attributed it to a cascade of security failures at Microsoft, and said Microsoft's security culture was inadequate and requires an overhaul. The stolen signing key allowed access to Exchange Online mailboxes of more than 500 people and 22 organizations, including senior U.S. officials.
facts.quote: Microsoft's security culture was inadequate and requires an overhaul.

sources.publisher: Cyber Safety Review Board (U.S. Department of Homeland Security / CISA)
sources.title: Review of the Summer 2023 Microsoft Exchange Online Intrusion
Cyber review board blames cascading Microsoft failures for Chinese hack
Cyber Safety Review Board finds Microsoft security culture 'inadequate,' calls for accountability

facts.claim: The CSRB found that as of its report Microsoft did not know how or when Storm-0558 obtained the signing key, and that Microsoft took months, and repeated prompting from the board, to amend a public blog post after concluding it lacked evidence the key had been exposed in a crash dump.
facts.quote: As of the date of this report, Microsoft does not know how or when Storm-0558 obtained the signing key.

facts.claim: Following OpenAI's recapitalization announced October 28, 2025, Microsoft holds an investment in OpenAI Group PBC valued at approximately $135 billion, roughly 27 percent on an as-converted diluted basis (down from 32.5 percent before recent funding rounds). Microsoft continues to account for its $13 billion of total funding commitments under the equity method, its IP rights to OpenAI models run through 2032, OpenAI contracted to buy an additional $250 billion of Azure services, and Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal as OpenAI's compute provider.
facts.quote: Following the recapitalization, Microsoft holds an investment in OpenAI Group PBC valued at approximately $135B, representing roughly 27% on an as-converted diluted basis

facts.claim: Microsoft won the Pentagon's $10 billion JEDI cloud contract in late 2019; the Pentagon cancelled JEDI in July 2021 and in December 2022 named Microsoft one of four providers on the $9 billion-ceiling Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability contract.
facts.quote: Microsoft had won JEDI in late 2019, and Amazon challenged that award, alleging that political interference may have affected the outcome.

sources.title: Pentagon Awards $9B Cloud Contract to Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Oracle

facts.claim: On September 25, 2025, Microsoft vice chair Brad Smith said the company had ceased and disabled a set of services, including cloud storage and AI services, to a unit within the Israel Ministry of Defense, after an external review led by Covington & Burling found evidence supporting elements of an August 2025 Guardian report that Unit 8200 used Azure to store and analyze civilian phone calls from the West Bank and Gaza. Microsoft said its cybersecurity work for Israel was not affected and the review was ongoing.
facts.quote: ceased and disabled a set of services to a unit within the Israel ministry of defense

sources.title: Microsoft cuts off Israel's Unit 8200 from cloud services after surveillance revelations
Israel/OPT: Microsoft terminates Israeli military's access to technology used to operate mass surveillance system in Gaza & the West Bank

facts.claim: On November 18, 2025, Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest up to $15 billion combined in Anthropic (up to $5 billion from Microsoft and up to $10 billion from Nvidia), and Anthropic committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity.
facts.quote: Anthropic agreed to buy $30 billion of computing capacity from Microsoft's Azure cloud service.

facts.claim: According to a Bloomberg analysis of federal lobbying filings, Microsoft spent about $9.36 million on U.S. federal lobbying in 2025, slightly less than in 2024. Axios put its quarterly spending at $2.4 million in Q1, $2 million in Q3 and $2.4 million in Q4 2025.
facts.quote: Amazon came next at about $17.89 million, Alphabet at $13.10 million, and Microsoft at $9.36 million.

sources.publisher: DeepLearning.AI (The Batch), relaying a Bloomberg analysis of federal lobbying filings
sources.title: Big AI Spends Big On Lobbying: Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia pour millions into government influence
